edits.content:
# L02 Context pressure recovery (depth half)

## Contract

`recoverContextPressure(snapshot, options)` projects four deterministic sections from an existing Working Context snapshot:

- goals
- unfinishedWork
- dependencies
- recentEvidence

The same snapshot and options produce the same SHA-256 digest. Recovery is opt-in and bounded by `maxDepth`; when `currentDepth` exceeds that bound the result is `depth-exceeded`, has no sections, and never claims completion.

## Accounting

Each section has `items`, `kept`, `dropped`, and `truncated`. Every source item is either kept or counted in `dropped`; consequently `kept + dropped` equals the source item count. `totalKept + totalDropped` is the total number of source items across the four sections.

An absent or empty snapshot is `unknown`, not `recovered`. All successful and unsuccessful results have `complete: false`.

## Safety

This is the depth half only. Handoff-chain depth, runtime handoff opt-in, loop fail-closed behavior, and subagent `maxSpawnDepth` remain unchanged. No defaults, locks, approvals, dependency configuration, or product behavior are modified.

# L02 context pressure recovery

The runtime exposes a bounded projection of the existing Working Context snapshot. It recovers goals, unfinished work, dependencies, and recent evidence in a stable order and returns a SHA-256 digest of the canonical projection.

Recovery never follows a nested snapshot. The caller supplies `maxDepth` and `currentDepth`; exceeding the limit returns `depth-exceeded` with `sections: null`. Missing or empty input returns `unknown`. The result always has `complete: false`.

Budgeting is explicit. Each section reports kept and dropped counts, and `truncated` is true whenever an item was not retained. No item is silently discarded: kept plus dropped equals the source count.

This document covers the context pressure recovery depth half. It does not change the handoff-chain implementation, runtime handoff opt-in, loop handling, subagent spawn limits, product defaults, locks, or approvals.
